newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends lower on weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends lower on weak demand.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower after buying sentiment remained weak in the current holiday season, despite emergence of some short-covering, traders said.

With most overseas consumers and even local producers on holiday, the only sale announced for the day was an 80-tonne cargo of SMR 20 for Dubai priced at 308.50 cents ($1.22) a kg for January shipment, traders said.
They said buyers remaining in the market were hunting for bargains while producers were seeking a premium because rains had reduced tapping and their stocks of raw materials.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted January RSS1 buyer at 318 ($1.26) a kg, down half cent from Monday. January SMR 20 buyer was quoted one cent lower at 308.50.
Dealers quoted the SMR CV at 363 cents, SMR L at 344, SMR 5 at 319, SMR 10 at 309, SMR 20 at 308 and drum latex at 237.
The INRO five-day moving average rose to 241.45 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Dec 16 from 240.52 on Dec 13. The daily indicator price jumped to 243.71 from 241.15.
